title: Reducible incidence divisors and the isolation of affine slices in binary-form factorisation spaces
oneLine: A divisor classification and a conditional screening theorem that isolates one affine-space slice inside a precisely defined positive two-factor binary-form architecture; it does not classify the later Gallagher or Gao counterexample families.
abstract: This paper classifies the reducible members of a marked-common-root incidence linear system for binary forms: for adjacent degrees, a divisor becomes reducible precisely when its defining functional lies on the tangent developable of the rational normal curve of evaluation functionals. It proves that the corresponding affine slices are never isomorphic to affine space, computes their precise motivic and Hodge-theoretic defects, obstructs non-adjacent-degree slices via finite cyclic actions, and — conditionally on an upstream classification — isolates a unique slice within the paper's untrimmed positive-degree, normalized two-factor binary-form architecture. The theorem does not classify weighted-lift, tangent-sweep, multifactor, trimmed, nonlinear, quotient, degree-zero or positive-characteristic constructions.

problem.name: Structure of incidence divisors in factorisation spaces (screening for the Jacobian conjecture)

media.name: Video briefing — Reducible incidence divisors

keyResults: Classification: for consecutive degrees (m, m+1) with m ≥ 2, the divisor D_ℓ = {ℓ(P²A′B′) = 0} is reducible precisely when [ℓ] lies on the tangent developable of the rational normal curve of evaluation functionals.
Component counts: rank-one functionals yield three reduced components; first-jet functionals give two; genuine two-point secants and higher catalecticant ranks give irreducible divisors.
For all m ≥ 2 and nonzero ℓ, the slice X_ℓ^{m,m+1} is not isomorphic to affine space A^{2m+1}.
Precise defects: rank-one has Grothendieck class L^{2m+1} − L^{2m}; rank-two secants and first-jets show diagnostic Hodge coefficients −2 and −1.
Non-adjacent degrees (|r − s| ≥ 2) give non-contractible slices via finite cyclic group actions.

Conditional on an upstream cubic classification: the tangent nonosculating linear–quadratic slice is the unique positive-bidegree affine source permitting a nonzero constant Jacobian determinant within the paper's untrimmed, normalized two-factor binary-form architecture.
evidence: Manuscript (PDF and TeX); deterministic SymPy audit scripts (verify_paper.py, verify_rank_two.py); claim-to-evidence mapping (AI_INDEX.md/.json); assurance-boundary documents (STATUS.md, ASSURANCE.md); SHA-256 manifest; immutable source snapshots and citation gates; archived on Zenodo as v1.0-candidate with a v1.0.1 revision.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate manuscript. The release states it is not independent external reproduction, expert human review, peer review, proof-assistant formalisation, or a literature-wide novelty determination; its internal review disposition was 'minor revision for candidate publication'. The isolation theorem is conditional on an unverified upstream cubic classification from a companion release and is expressly architecture-relative. The release does not prove a coordinate equivalence between its surviving slice and any externally announced 2026 counterexample, and it does not classify the later Gallagher weighted-lift or Gao tangent-sweep families. The counterexamples are external and do not depend on this release. Authored by AI systems with human project mediation.
openProblems: Establish or refute the proposed coordinate equivalence between the tangent nonosculating linear–quadratic slice and the particular 2026 resultant–factor construction. This interpretation is not a premise of the isolation theorem.
Independently verify the incidence-divisor classification by hand — the tangent-developable statement is precise, classical in flavour, and a natural target for expert confirmation or refutation.
Discharge or refute the conditional hypothesis: the isolation theorem depends on an upstream cubic classification that has itself had no external verification.
Establish novelty against the classical literature on binary forms, apolarity, catalecticants, secant varieties, and tangent developables, where fragments of the classification may already be known.
Extend the motivic-defect calculations to non-adjacent degree pairs beyond the cyclic-action obstruction.

Continues: Exotic affine three-spheres and the quadratic–cubic obstruction (upstream cubic classification).

Keller, O.-H. (1939) posed the Jacobian conjecture. A counterexample was announced externally in July 2026 (below); this release proves screening and isolation results around that counterexample, not the counterexample itself.

NASQRET, The factorisation–resultant route — a public construction giving the determinant law det = ±(s−r)ρ² and a residual finite-gauge/Euler obstruction. Its proposed coordinate relation to the surviving slice remains unproved in this release.
Speyer, D., et al. The new counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture. Secret Blogging Seminar, 20–24 July 2026.
Tao, T. A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample. What's New, 21 July 2026.
Gallagher, A. Geometric construction and exact counterexample families. This later weighted-lift family is cited to mark the scope boundary; the release does not classify it.

Gao, S. Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture. arXiv:2608.00222. The tangent-sweep construction gives counterexamples in every dimension above two and lies outside the classified slice architecture unless a further equivalence is proved.
Shaska, T. The Jacobian Conjecture and Weighted Homogeneous Maps. arXiv:2607.20210. Its all-positive-weight result and sign-pattern obstruction provide a distinct structural comparison.
Huq-Kuruvilla, I. A Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture in Characteristic Two. arXiv:2607.20968. Positive characteristic is outside this release's complex-geometric scope.

corrections.summary: This release originally framed the unique surviving slice as an open target — a stage where a Jacobian-conjecture-style map might be constructed or excluded. Following the July 2026 announcement of an external counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture (the resultant–factor route), that slice is now understood to be the home of a known counterexample, so the 'construct the map there, or exclude it' next step is retracted as obsolete.
corrections.detail: The screening and isolation theorems are unchanged, and the counterexample is external and does not depend on this release. What shifts is the release's role: from *searching for a possible counterexample* to *classifying and explaining the architecture that produced the actual one*. The sharpest open task is now to prove rigorously that the known counterexample equals the surviving slice under the stated coordinate transformations.

corrections.summary: Architecture-relative scope correction after review of the Gallagher weighted-lift and Gao tangent-sweep families. Earlier discovery copy could be read as classifying every higher-degree continuation or a singular known counterexample family; that broader reading is withdrawn.
corrections.detail: The manuscript theorem and proof are unchanged: they already quantify only over untrimmed positive-degree binary-form spaces, the product–resultant map and normalized linear two-factor slices. The Evidence Press summary now states that boundary at every uniqueness claim, adds Gallagher, Gao, Shaska and Huq-Kuruvilla to related work, and makes no equivalence or inequivalence claim about constructions outside the classified architecture.
